1) Question: A student is studying for an exam and wants to improve their memory retention. They have heard that taking breaks during study sessions can help with this. However, they also know that cramming all night before the exam may lead to better grades. Based on this information, what would be the best approach for the student to take?

Answer 1: Taking regular breaks during long study sessions is more beneficial for improving memory retention than cramming the night before an exam. This allows the brain to process and consolidate information over time rather than trying to absorb everything at once.
Follow up question 1: Why might cramming lead to higher grades even though it may not be as effective for memory retention?
Answer 2: Cramming may result in short term memorization of information, but it does not allow for deep understanding or critical thinking skills to develop. Therefore, students who cram may perform well on exams that require rote memorization, but struggle with exams that test comprehension and application of knowledge.

A. Cotrimoxazole
B. Azithromycin
C. Ampicillin
D. Chloroquine
subject: Pharmacology
full_response:
Answer: A. Cotrimoxazole
A paediatrician was called for attending a new born baby in the labour ward. The serum unconjugated bilirubin of this baby was 33 mg/dL. Which of the following drug taken by mother in late 3rd trimester may have lead to this problem?
A. Cotrimoxazole
B. Azithromycin
C. Ampicillin
D. Chloroquine
Answer: A. Cotrimoxazole
Answer: A. Cotrimoxazole
Explanation: Bilirubin given in question is very high; Bilirubin binds to Albumin in blood, so when any drug displaces bilirubin from albumin, it can lead to increased free bilirubin. Cotrimoxazole is a combination of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole (a sulfonamide). Sulfonamides (acidic drugs) can displace bilirubin from albumin resulting in excessive free bilirubin. This can cross blood brain barrier in newborn babies which can cause Kernicterus; hence avoided in pregnancy.

A 38-years old patient who had a total abdominal hysterectomy presents 2 months postop complaining of leakage of urine from the vagina. On examination, no fistula can be identified. Dilute methylene blue (100mL) is injected into the bladder through a Foley catheter and a tampon is placed in the vagina. The patient is asked to walk for about 15 minutes, after which the patient is found to be wet, but there is no blue stain anywhere on the tampon. Which of the following is true:-
A. 100mL was probably not enough methylene blue, and the test should be repeated with a higher volume
B. The patient probably has stress incontinence not a fistula
C. The patient probably has a ureterovaginal fistula
D. The patient most likely has small apical vesicovaginal fistula that was too small to leak the dye in 15 minutes
subject: Gynaecology & Obstetrics
full_response:
Answer: C. The patient probably has a ureterovaginal fistula
Explanation: Methylene blue Swab Test-- A catheter is introduced into the bladder through the urethra, The vaginal cavity is packed with three sterile swabs, 50-100 mL of dilute methylene blue dye is injected into the bladder through the catheter. If there is a fistulous connection between the bladder and the vagina, the dye will leak out of the vagina and stain the swabs. This test is positive if the swab turns blue within 10 minutes. In this case, the patient did not have any blue staining on the swamp, indicating that there is an absence of a fistular connection between bladder and vagina. Therefore, the diagnosis is ureterso-vaginal fistulae.

B. IUGR
C. IUD

Which of the following instructions should be given to a lactating mother regarding drug usage?
A. No advice is required as most of the drugs are secreted negligibly in the milk
B. Take drugs with longer half-life
C. Tell her to feed the baby just before next dose
D. Do not feed the baby if you are consuming any drug

full_response:

C. Tell the mother to feed when it is least efficacious
D. Lactate Just before she take the next dose, when the plasma concentration of drug would be least.
Answer: D. Lactate Just before she take the next dose, when the plasma concentration of drug would be least.
Explanation: Just before the next dose, the plasma concentration of drug is minimum; so it is relatively safer to feed at that time. Some drugs are secreted significantly in milk. There is no relation between half-life of a drug and its milk secretion ; So, long half life drugs may also come in milk. Not all the drugs are harmful or significantly secreted in milk so feed should not be stopped.
